text: The first micro-world may include households with different water-access privileges to make infrastructure inequality causal.
Household forms in the fixture deliberately vary; no single patrilocal joint-family template is enforced.
Illness or material uncertainty may open a ritual decision affordance with real resource/time cost, without predetermining that every actor chooses it.
V0.1 grain/oil/silver/ritual quantities are abstract resource units chosen only to exercise scarcity, conservation, debt, and validation mechanics.
Routine household consumption and weekly receipts are deterministic fixture mechanics, not reconstructed Ugaritic daily rations or wages.
Local fixture messages use integer-day travel delays to exercise asynchronous information; exact route speeds are not yet historical calibrations.

A household resource-security scene is triggered only when deterministic projection over one configured weekly receipt cycle shows that full daily grain need cannot be met on a future day; projection uses current stock, fixture daily need, scheduled receipt timing, and fixture receipt amount.

The two initial expected-arrival reports are explicit simulation circumstances used to exercise stale, incomplete, and discordant information; they do not assert a historically specific Ugaritic shipment, cargo, route, or outcome.

A one-day outside porter-work opportunity for P16 on or after fixture day 14, with a 1.0 abstract-grain household receipt after completion, exists only to exercise household labor-priority negotiation. Its timing, duration, compensation, and contract form are simulation fixtures, not reconstructed Ugaritic wages or employment practice.

A temporary shared-water-point disruption on or after fixture day 18 and a P2↔P6 neighbor tie are simulation circumstances used to exercise negotiation across unequal household water access. The disruption, exact access duration, neighbor pairing, and procedure are not asserted as historical Ugaritic events or law.

The Ugarit micro-world uses a 360-day Mediterranean dry-farming calendar with simulation day 0 placed at modeled cereal harvest. Seasonal ordering and labor bottlenecks are research-constrained; exact phase boundaries and day alignment are engineering calibration, not an attested Ugaritic date conversion.

Recurring textile and metalwork cycles consume abstract fiber/metal/fuel inputs and produce abstract textile/metal goods so specialist occupations have material dependencies. Quantities and conversion ratios are engineering calibration, not reconstructed production rates.

Household ritual observance and selected communal rite/feast checkpoints recur on model-owned cadences and consume abstract ritual/food resources. Ugaritic household religion and communal drinking/feasting are research-supported; exact dates, frequencies, and contribution quantities are not claimed as historical reconstruction.

A recurring palace labor request is used to test the opportunity cost of institutional extraction during seasonal household labor bottlenecks. The existence of institutional labor obligations is research-supported; cadence, duration, and the bounded rescheduling mechanism are engineering calibration rather than reconstructed Ugaritic corvee procedure.

Recurring Ugaritic port/market cycles and delayed exchange commitments model occupational interaction among merchants, sailors, porters, market traders, scribes and interpreters. Exchange amounts, weighed-metal-to-goods ratio, and transit delay are engineering calibration and are not historical price, volume, or profit-rate claims.

A resource supplied after a direct social request may be represented as open-ended reciprocal social credit rather than a free gift or a fixed-price/interest debt. The reciprocity mechanism is research-supported; the specific obligation creation and absence of a fixed maturity are simulation choices, not reconstructed Ugaritic contract terms.

Routine weekly household grain provisioning is calibrated to exactly seven configured daily needs so the no-shock baseline is materially neutral rather than structurally enriching or impoverishing households. This is an engineering stability baseline, not a reconstructed Ugaritic production, ration, wage, or income rate; material gains/losses should arise from modeled work, exchange, obligations, ritual, shocks, and decisions.

An open reciprocal social-credit obligation may become eligible for voluntary return after 30 simulation days when the obligor household has suitable occupational output. The first craft implementation suggests 0.3 abstract finished-metalwork units as a return. Timing and amount are engineering calibration and do not claim a historical price, equivalence, or repayment term.

After at least two completed fixture trade exchanges, the merchant household's lower-risk account partner may initiate a household silver-reserve negotiation. Earliest eligibility, the one-standard-commitment reserve calculation, and the exact floor are engineering calibration; the modeled mechanism is that household strategy can constrain an individual's discretionary trade exposure.

Niqmepa may become eligible to request recognition as a craft worker only after at least 91 simulation days, twelve recorded apprenticeship work cycles, and accumulated workshop output. Progression changes his simulation role to a dependent recognized craft worker within the same workshop household. Timing, production threshold, legal-status label, and post-progression production quantities are engineering calibration, not reconstructed Ugaritic apprenticeship law, guild rank, or duration.

Selected household/economic proposal scenes expose one bounded informal mediation opportunity after direct disagreement. The engine records relationship strain on refusal and can reopen the proposal through an abstract kin/patron/elder mediation interface; the exact mediator identity, settlement terms, authority, and Ugaritic procedure remain unspecified unless later evidence supports them.

Kothar (P16) and Šapšu (P10) become eligible for a first bounded marriage-discussion opportunity at the modeled day-150 communal feast if both remain alive, available, and unmarried. The pairing, timing, and feast introduction are engineering fixtures used to exercise multi-household marriage negotiation; they are not claims about historical individuals, a historical marriage, or Ugaritic matchmaking procedure.

The first marriage negotiation restricts residence to either the existing H-WIDOW or H-RITUAL household and may preserve a continuing care obligation from P16 to P15. These bounded terms are engineering choices for causal household testing and do not claim a universal Ugaritic patrilocal, matrilocal, dowry, bridewealth, inheritance, or elder-care rule.

From simulation day 141, relevant agricultural workers can generate a separate seasonal_produce surplus during the grape/olive/field-preparation phase; exposed surplus can suffer modeled storage loss and can be preserved into stored_seasonal_goods. Production amounts, thresholds, preservation yield, and storage-loss percentage are engineering calibration only and are deliberately separate from neutral staple grain provisioning.

From v007, neutral routine grain provisioning follows current living household composition. Each person carries the per-person daily fixture share implied by their day-0 household; the receiving household consumes and receives that share after residence change. This is an engineering conservation model, not a historical ration, wage, dependency weight, or consumption estimate.

The P16→P15 continuing-care term from the accepted marriage can generate periodic concrete support needs. Fulfilled care is remembered and, after repeated fulfillment, may open a non-binding P15 property-preference review. Timing, support task, threshold, and preference form are simulation fixtures; no Ugaritic inheritance rule or automatic transfer is asserted.

During the v007 early-rains/sowing phase, H-FARM controls a fixture draft-team access option while H-DEPEND must negotiate for one bounded service opportunity. The household pairing, ownership/access asymmetry, service timing, and sowing-progress quantities are engineering fixtures used to make sowing access socially causal; they are not reconstructed Ugaritic livestock ownership or plowing rates.

From v008, the H-FARM fixture draft team has an abstract condition state that accumulates a first modeled wet-winter maintenance backlog across weekly cycles until the episode is resolved. If condition falls far enough, P1 may ask P13 to answer the already-recorded sowing favor with one bounded winter care/maintenance labor service. Timing, condition values, household pairing, labor duration, and restoration amount are engineering fixtures; no Ugaritic animal-care rate, plowing contract, or fixed exchange equivalence is asserted.

From v008, when a newly created reciprocal social-credit obligation seals the originating support amount, a later finished-metalwork return suggestion is capped at the lesser of 0.3 fixture units and that originating support amount. This conservative limiter prevents a shrinking fixture support transfer from mechanically producing a larger suggested return; it is not a historical price, interest rate, exchange rate, or equivalence claim.

From v009, a supply-constrained craft household may choose a bounded local remelting fallback that consumes finished_metalwork and recovers a smaller amount of raw metal. The first fixture permits 0.20 finished_metalwork to yield 0.12 metal. The quantities and 60% recovery ratio are engineering calibration only, not a historical Ugaritic recovery rate or value equivalence.

From v009, after the accepted P3→P7 scarcity refusal, P7 may seek an alternate raw-metal source only through a modeled social/information path. P3 can introduce harbor contact P11; P11 privately knows one fixture market lead involving P12; P7 must inquire, receive the delayed report, request terms from P12, and independently accept any offered exchange. The lead, people chosen, 0.30-silver/0.30-metal terms and three-day delivery are engineering fixtures, not a historical Ugaritic shipment or price.

From v010, H-CRAFT begins with a finite abstract fuel_feedstock reserve that can be deliberately converted into charcoal when workshop fuel becomes limiting. The first fixture converts 0.40 fuel_feedstock into 0.50 charcoal. Feedstock quantity, conversion ratio, timing, and household ownership are engineering calibration only; they are not historical charcoal yields, woodland-use rates, or Ugaritic fuel accounts.

From v010, after the first alternate metal lot has completed, a later P12 market update can report one bounded disruption: only 0.18 usable metal is available for 0.30 silver after five days because of temporary harbor/weather handling loss and delay. The specific timing, people, lot size, loss, price, and delay are simulation fixtures used to test network resilience; they are not a historical Ugaritic cargo event or probability estimate.

From v011, when H-CRAFT is at or below one remaining 0.40-unit fuel-feedstock preparation batch, P7 may ask co-located porter/seasonal worker P16 for one bounded local fuel-haul service. If accepted, one day later 0.20 silver moves H-CRAFT→H-WIDOW and 0.80 external local fuel_feedstock enters H-CRAFT. Pairing, recurrence by agricultural phase, payment, duration and quantity are engineering fixtures, not a historical Ugaritic wage, woodland yield or transport contract.

From v011, after the accepted v010 disrupted lot, P12 privately knows that the same fixture contact currently has no additional usable raw-metal lot. P7 must ask again and receive that delayed report before acting on unavailability. Once learned, a low-metal workshop can reopen a bounded recycling-or-wait decision by 14-day episode bucket. The no-lot state, duration and recurrence are engineering fixtures, not a historical market event or frequency claim.

From v012, the first otherwise-viable P7 master metalwork cycle after day 421 can suffer one bounded fixture tool/mold failure before production. The failure sets abstract workshop_tool_condition to 0 and blocks that cycle. P7 may repair by sacrificing 0.10 finished_metalwork and one modeled day; repair completion restores condition to 1.0. Trigger timing, condition scale, repair material and duration are engineering fixtures, not historical failure or repair rates.

From v013, one bounded dry-summer local moisture/rain exposure episode can threaten only exposed seasonal_produce in H-FARM and H-DEPEND. Each household senior may protect the exposed stock by committing one modeled household labor day, reducing the fixture extra-loss fraction from 0.30 to 0.05; or accept the 0.30 extra loss. The day, households, fractions, labor cost, and protective effectiveness are engineering fixtures, not a historical Ugaritic weather event or spoilage rate. Neutral staple grain and stored_seasonal_goods are never affected by this fixture.

From v014, after Bat-Rapiu's care-informed non-binding property preference has remained active and the H-WIDOW household includes married-in adult Šapšu, Bat-Rapiu may propose earmarking 0.80 silver for household-property maintenance with Kothar as proposed steward. Šapšu may accept, refuse, or counter with a smaller amount and joint approval; Bat-Rapiu reviews any counter; Kothar must separately consent before any reserve is established. Strict fixture terms may settle at 0.40 silver. People, timing, amounts, approval structure and reserve representation are engineering fixtures, not a historical Ugaritic property rule, inheritance transfer, or legal office.
